1.why: All six screens are static, card-based layouts with no animations, moving images, or pop-up dialogs visible.

2.why: Bold headings and solid blue primary buttons stand out clearly, but the critical consent checkbox in step 4 is tiny and oddly placed inside a wide empty box.

3.why: Each screen presents one task in a single column, though the persistent Logs panel and demo text add some clutter to scan past.

4.why: The flow requires four sequential steps plus two separate codes (a 64-character recovery code and a security code), though the codes are displayed on screen so recall is partly offloaded.

5.why: No password manager integration, autofill hints, or 'remember me' option appear anywhere; only a demo-prefilled recovery code field is shown.

6.why: There are no saved accounts, recognizable prefilled identity items, or familiar-item cues; the only prefilled content is the simulated test code.

7.why: Instruction text is short and plain, but technical log jargon ('SIMULATED MFA DELIVERY', 'Plaintext password was not logged') and the long hex code reduce overall readability.

8.why: No error messages appear in any of the six steps, so the claim that they describe problems and fixes is not supported by what is observed.

9.why: The demo displays the exact test recovery code to copy, functioning as an example, but input fields themselves have no placeholder examples or format guidance.

10.why: Only a single code-based recovery path exists; no alternative login choices such as password or face login are offered at all.

11.why: Every screen presents essentially one action (one field, one button), so the user is never confronted with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Each action is explicitly confirmed in the Logs and UI ('Recovery code verified', 'MFA verification completed', final green 'Recovery complete' message).

13.why: Each step includes a brief instruction line and a persistent 'Stay safe' tips panel, though there is no contextual help or tooltip for individual fields.

14.why: No resend-code, back, or retry affordances are visible on any screen, so recovery from a mistake is not visibly supported.

15.why: The header, card layout, 'Stay safe' panel, and Logs panel remain identical across all six steps, providing a highly consistent, learnable design.
